paper.title: An Asymptotically Optimal Primal-Dual Incremental Algorithm for Contextual Linear Bandits

settings.name_in_paper: Contextual linear bandit (finite contexts, finite arms, Gaussian noise)
unmapped: Finite context set X drawn i.i.d. from distribution rho with rho(x) >= rho_min > 0 for all contexts
Per-round feature set is {phi(X_t,a): a in A}, varying with the i.i.d. context
Unique optimal arm required in each context
Comparator is the best arm in each context
settings.definition_quote: At each time step $t \in \mathbb{N}$, the learner observes a context $X_t\in\X$ drawn i.i.d.\ from a context distribution $\rho$, it pulls an arm $A_t\in\A$, and it receives a reward $Y_{t} = \phi(X_t,A_t)^\transp\theta^\star + \xi_t$ ... The realizable parameters belong to a compact subset $\Theta$ of $\R^d$ such that $\|\theta\|_2 \leq B$ ... features are bounded, i.e., $\| \phi(x,a) \|_2 \leq L$ ... $\rho(x) \geq \rho_{\min} > 0$ ... $\theta^\star$ has a unique optimal arm in each context

bound.expression_latex: asymptotically optimal with the same constant as in the lower bound of Prop. 1, i.e. \limsup R_n/\log n \le v^\star(\theta^\star)

conditions: Assumption 1: ||theta|| <= B, ||phi(x,a)|| <= L, rho(x) >= rho_min > 0, unique optimal arm per context

source.label: thm:regret.bound
source.quote: If \algo is run with confidence values $\beta_{t-1} = c_{n,1/n}$ and $\gamma_t = c_{n,1/S_t^2}$ ... learning rates $\alpha_k^\lambda = \alpha_k^\omega = 1/\sqrt{p_k}$ and increasing sequences $z_k = z_0 e^k$ and $p_k = z_k e^{2k}$, for some $z_0 \geq 1$, then it is \textbf{asymptotically optimal} with the same constant as in the lower bound of Prop.~\ref{p:lower.bound}.

results.notes: Asymptotic optimality matches the cited lower bound of Proposition 1. The constant v* is written C_lin in the canonical vocabulary but is declared here as v_star. Regret is defined through mean gaps, so it is recorded as pseudo-regret.

symbols.c_n: confidence radius c_{n,1/n} = O(log n + d log log n) from Theorem 1
symbols.C_const: v* B^2 L^2/sigma^2 + lin_{>=0}(L, B, z_0 (z_underline/z_0)^3, (z_bar/z_0)^2)

conditions: Assumption 1: ||theta|| <= B, ||phi(x,a)|| <= L, rho(x) >= rho_min > 0, unique optimal arm per context

source.label: thm:regret.bound
source.quote: Furthermore, for any finite $n$ the regret of \algo is bounded as \E[R_n(\theta^\star)] \leq v^\star(\theta^\star) \frac{c_{n,1/n}}{2\sigma^2} + C_{\log} (\log\log n)^{\frac{1}{2}}(\log n)^{\frac{3}{4}} + C_{\mathrm{const}}, where $C_{\log} = lin_{\geq 0}(v^\star(\theta^\star),|\X|,L^2,B^2,\sqrt{d},1/\sigma^2)$ and $C_{\mathrm{const}} = v^\star(\theta^\star)\frac{B^2L^2}{\sigma^2}+ lin_{\geq 0 }(L,B, z_0 (\sfrac{\underline{z}(\theta^\star)}{z_0})^{3}, (\sfrac{\wb{z}(\theta^\star)}{z_0})^2)$.

results.notes: The constants are given only through 'lin' functions, i.e. up to unspecified nonnegative coefficients. c_{n,1/n} is O(log n + d log log n). |X| is M_ctx. The paper says the bound depends only logarithmically on |A|.

symbols.lambda_max: maximum Lagrange multiplier used by SOLID

conditions: Assumption 1: ||theta|| <= B, ||phi(x,a)|| <= L, rho(x) >= rho_min > 0, unique optimal arm per context

source.label: th:worst-case
source.quote: Let $z_k$ be arbitrary, $p_k = e^{rk}$ for some constant $r \geq 1$, and the other parameters be the same as in Thm.~\ref{thm:regret.bound}. Then, for any $n$ the regret of \algo is bounded as \E[R_n(\theta^\star)] \leq 12BL\pi^2C_{\lambda_{\max}} + \frac{2e^r\left(\lambda_{\max}^2 + \log|\A|\right)}{r}\sqrt{n} + C_{\mathrm{sqrt}} C_{\lambda_{\max}}\log (n) \sqrt{dn}, where $C_{\mathrm{sqrt}} = lin_{\geq 0}(|\X| + \sqrt{d}, B, L)$ and $C_{\lambda_{\max}} := \left(1 + \frac{\lambda_{\max}BL}{\sigma^2}\right)$.

results.notes: B is mapped to S and L to L_feat. The paper summarises this bound as O~((sqrt(d) + |X|) sqrt(dn) + log|A| sqrt(n)), which it says is minimax optimal when |X| <= sqrt(d).
